key_insight: An LLM can help generate a human-readable formal proof of the irrationality of 2, but the proof is still validated end-to-end by the LPTP theorem prover.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical workflow for pairing language models with logic-program theorem proving to accelerate formal verification while preserving proof correctness.
method: Start from basic pure logic-program predicate definitions.
Use LPTP natural-deduction proof language to sketch the classic irrationality proof.
Iteratively interact with an LLM, then fully proof-check the generated result in LPTP.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a single case study: the authors obtained a complete formal proof, partially generated by an LLM and fully checked by LPTP.
watch_item: The result is demonstrated on one classic theorem, so broader reliability on more complex proofs or different logic-program settings remains unproven.
paper_title: Case study: proving sqrt(2) irrational with LPTP and an LLM
